concept.name: Time price opportunity
concept.definition: The atomic unit of a Market Profile chart: one TPO records that the market had the opportunity to trade at a given price during a given time bracket (conventionally 30 minutes). Each bracket is assigned a letter, and that letter is stamped at every price the market touched during the bracket.
concept.intuition: A TPO is one half-hour 'vote' for a price — the more brackets that traded at a level, the more time the market accepted it.
concept.mechanics: The session is split into sequential brackets (A, B, C…); for each price traded within a bracket, that bracket's letter is added to the price's row, so row length measures time-at-price and the whole array forms the profile distribution.
concept.failure_modes: TPO counts measure time, not volume — a price briefly visited in many brackets can outrank a price where most contracts actually traded; bracket size and session boundaries are conventions that change the picture.
concept.misconceptions: A TPO is not a trade or a volume unit; rows of letters show opportunity (time at price), which is why the same session's TPO POC and volume POC can sit at different prices.
concept.example: If ES trades at 4,520 during brackets A, C, and D, that price's row holds three TPO letters; the row with the most letters by day's end is the point of control.
